properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 6 to 10 feet for south and
southwestern-facing beaches and 4 to 7 feet for west-facing
beaches. Strong and dangerous rip and longshore currents. Minor
coastal flooding from a combination of high surf and high
astronomical tides.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
coastal areas.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Saturday morning to 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Predicted tides for La Jolla, CA:
Sat, Sep 5 2026: 6.0 feet at 4:48 PM PDT
Sun, Sep 6 2026: 6.3 feet at 6:03 PM PDT
Mon, Sep 7 2026: 6.7 feet at 7:03 PM PDT
Tue, Sep 8 2026: 6.8 feet at 7:54 PM PDT

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions. Always swim near a lifeguard. Stay off
of sea walls and jetties. Waves will occasionally run farther up
the beach than expected, especially during high and rising tides;
set up farther back from the ocean and do not turn your back on
the ocean.

properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Central Interior-Nenana-Two Rivers-Middle Yukon Valley-Upper Koyukuk
Valley-Upper Chena River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area-Goldstream
Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Dalton Highway
Summits-Chatanika River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain South
of the Yukon River-Eielson AFB and Salcha

Areas of 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall are expected over the next 48
hours due to an atmospheric river. Average return intervals of 2 to 5
years is possible throughout much of the central and western interior
through the weekend. Isolated areas could potentially see heavy
rainfall more in line with 10 to even 25 year return intervals,
resulting in significant rises in the smaller headwater streams that
feed the Koyukuk and Middle Yukon Rivers. While there are no
immediate concerns for the main stem rivers in the area, they will
also see significant rises in water levels through the week as a
result of the expected heavy rainfall with sandbars potentially
becoming covered with water.

Across the Chena River basin, moderate to heavy rainfall of up to 1.5
inches is expected. This will also result in rises along the Chena
and Little Chena rivers. At this time flooding is not expected, but
should the focus for heaviest rainfall shift further east with time,
this could change.

Rainfall rates are expected to decrease by Sunday afternoon across
most of the area.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

areas, Adams, Bedford, Blair, Cambria, Cameron, Clearfield,
Columbia, Cumberland, Dauphin, Elk, Franklin, Fulton, Huntingdon,

Potter, Schuylkill, Snyder, Somerset, Southern Centre, Southern

York.

afternoon hours today, before the thunderstorms greatly increase

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move into Western Alaska Wednesday evening into Thursday, with
widespread rain and gusty winds expected. Water levels late
Thursday through Saturday morning could rise 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line along the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...Late Thursday September 3 through Saturday September 5.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. Heavy rain and
gusty winds could make travel difficult at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels are expected to peak late
Thursday into early Friday and again Saturday morning. Gusty
east/southeast winds Wednesday night will shift to the
south/southwest Thursday into Friday, leading to more onshore
flow and the potential for higher water levels. Strongest wind
gusts across the West Coast will peak on Thursday around 30 to
50 mph, with around 0.50 to 1.25 inches of rain expected through
Thursday night. Winds will be lighter Friday and Saturday, but
will remain onshore.

.Strong southwest winds will develop Wednesday as a cold front tracks
eastward and stalls along the Continental Divide. Winds will peak
each afternoon and early evening. Winds will remain elevated
Wednesday night, especially across midslopes and ridgetops, with poor
humidity recoveries.

The National Weather Service in Missoula MT has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 111.

* TIMING...From noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 20 to 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Make and maintain your go kit. Is it ready to go? Are there any
materials you need to refresh? Visit ready.gov/kit.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 1 at 9:27AM CDT until September 5 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Huntsville AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values reaching 105-109 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northeast, and northwest Alabama
and southern middle Tennessee.

* WHEN...From 11 AM Wednesday to 8 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM CDT SATURDAY
